rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit is a blessing from God, not part of God; Islahi says this clarification counters a major source of waḥdat al-wujūd.
rows.anchor: the spirit is from God and in fact from among the blessings of God. It does not mean that it is something part of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human development included an animal-like phase without intellect or insight; taswiyah perfected the external self and breathing the spirit perfected the inner self.
rows.anchor: a phase did pass on man when he was uncouth like animals and devoid of intellect and insight.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should reflect on each stage of creation, show gratitude through every part of the body, and use their abilities to please God; few do so.
rows.anchor: man should reflect on all these stages of his creation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave people sight, hearing, and intellect to recognize His power, wisdom, mercy, and providence, infer the world's purpose, and expect accountability and judgment.
rows.anchor: the Almighty had blessed man with the faculties of sight, hearing and intellect for a certain reason

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite witnessing signs of God's power, people mock the resurrection by asking whether they will be recreated after decaying into earth.
rows.anchor: Once We are lost into the earth, shall we be created again?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their doubts are excuses: they resist being brought before God and held accountable because that prospect weighs on them, so they fabricate objections.
rows.anchor: these people are not willing to accept the fact they will one day be brought forth before God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may use one objection as cover for denying something they cannot directly reject; Arab idolaters raised doubts about the Hereafter to evade its obligations, then invented deities and intercessors to escape its consequences.
rows.anchor: a person wants to negate something else but uses another thing as an excuse to negate it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An angel appointed over each person takes the soul at death; the deceased remains in God's sight, and God will raise each person and bring them before Him under angelic custody.
rows.anchor: his soul is claimed by an angel who is deputed by God on every person.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return is to the one God, not to alleged deities or intercessors, who will not exist on that day; God alone judges everyone.
rows.anchor: no one should remain in the misconception that when he dies he will be brought forth to his alleged deities and intercessors.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the address is to the Prophet, he would witness their helplessness at judgment in a degree beyond what he can imagine today.
rows.anchor: The implication is that the Prophet (sws) would have seen their helplessness at that time which he cannot even imagine today.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading that the address is to the Prophet, the conditional sentence's suppressed result is eloquent: he would witness a helplessness beyond what he can imagine now.
rows.anchor: The answer to this conditional clause is suppressed and there is much eloquence in this suppression.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At judgment, the wrongdoers will admit that they now see and hear the truth, and ask to return for the chance to do good deeds.
rows.anchor: at that time everyone of these wrongdoers will confess that they fully see and accept and that they may be allowed to return

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their compelled acknowledgment after witnessing the Hereafter is useless; God could have guided everyone from birth, but instead made guidance a test of choosing faith through insight or following Satan and desire.
rows.anchor: regarding guidance He gave a choice to people. The purpose was that He wanted to test people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that Hell will be filled with Satan's followers recalls God's answer to Satan's challenge, which Islahi notes is stated in several Qur'anic passages.
rows.anchor: This has been mentioned at many places in the Qur’ān. In Sūrah Ṣu‘ad, the words are:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's challenge and God's verdict mean that the period for apology has ended: human free choice between God and Satan was the test of worldly life, and people now face its consequences.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has granted man the free will to choose between God and Satan. This was his test in the life of the previous world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here nasiya means to ignore or take no notice: because people ignored the Day of Judgment, God ignores their pleas, and their eternal punishment is the result of their deeds, not injustice.
rows.anchor: the word نسي also means “to ignore” and “to take no notice of something or someone.” Here it is used in precisely this meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding section explains why people evaded faith in the Qur'an; the succeeding verses describe believers and their reward, as well as opponents' worldly and next-world fate.
rows.anchor: The previous section of verses has outlined the reasons on account of which people were evading to profess faith in the Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone sustains the heavens and earth and makes the universe useful to people; this should end human arrogance and prompt gratitude and obedience in using His favors.
rows.anchor: Nothing of this universe is providing benefit out of its own accord. It is doing so at the behest of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi links this lesson to the paired next sūrah, Fāṭir, citing its statement that God holds the heavens and earth from falling.
rows.anchor: This very topic is mentioned in Sūrah Fāt@ir, the next sūrah which occurs as the pair of this sūrah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens-and-earth sign supports the Qur'an's invitation for a truth-seeker who learns from others and has an inclined heart; signs do not affect people lacking those qualities.
rows.anchor: if they had reflected on this aspect of the heavens and the earth then they would have found a great argument

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David and Solomon received a kingdom, knowledge, wisdom, and many blessings without becoming arrogant; they remained grateful and obedient, so God continued increasing His favors.
rows.anchor: They never became arrogant and rebellious after receiving these favours; in fact, they continued to remain thankful and obedient to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Sheba had fertile, populated territory but grew arrogant and unruly; God routed them with a storm, leaving them a tale of the ancients.
rows.anchor: they became arrogant and unruly after receiving it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The examples confront affluent, arrogant Quraysh with a choice: follow David and Solomon to merit favor, or follow Sheba and incur God's wrath.
rows.anchor: Both these examples are presented before the affluent and arrogant among the Quraysh.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since divine reward and punishment already operate in this world, the examples challenge people to explain why they consider them improbable in the next.
rows.anchor: if God’s law of reward and punishment comes into play in this world, why do they consider it to be improbable in the next world.
